# Add OpenAI `gpt-realtime-2` as a third real voice engine

## Context

Tsubaki already has two real voice engines behind a provider-agnostic `SessionApi`:
**ElevenLabs** (`@elevenlabs/react`, WebRTC, managed) and **xAI Grok** (raw WebSocket +
ephemeral client-secret + hand-rolled PCM pipeline). The `openai` provider in
`lib/data.ts` exists today but has **no `engine`**, so it runs the design's mock lifecycle.

Goal: make the OpenAI provider a **real** engine using model `gpt-realtime-2`, wired into
the same `SessionApi` so the UI (orb, bars, captions, transcript, controls) is unchanged.

**Design decision (resolved):** connect via **WebRTC with an ephemeral token**, not the
"unified interface" (which would put our server in every session's critical path) and not
WebSocket (OpenAI explicitly discourages WS for browser playback). This choice means:

- The token route is a near-exact clone of the existing `app/api/xai/token/route.ts`,
  just pointed at OpenAI's `client_secrets` endpoint.
- WebRTC's `RTCPeerConnection` handles **all** audio — mic capture, playback, jitter
  buffering, and barge-in truncation — so the new hook is **much smaller** than
  `use-xai-session.ts` and needs **no `openai-audio.ts` PCM pipeline at all**.
- OpenAI's realtime events are the same family xAI already speaks, so the
  event→`CallState` mapping ports over directly. Events/state ride the `oai-events`
  **data channel**; audio rides the media tracks.

## Approach

Mirror the xAI integration's *shape* (a custom hook with the same interface as
`XaiSession`, plus a per-persona config module and a token-mint route), but swap the
transport to WebRTC.

### New files

**1. `app/api/openai/token/route.ts`** — clone of `app/api/xai/token/route.ts`.
- `POST` reads `process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY` (via fnox; never client-visible).
- Calls `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/client_secrets` with
  `Authorization: Bearer ${OPENAI_API_KEY}`, `Content-Type: application/json`, body

Verified end-to-end in Chrome, with one real bug found and fixed along the way.

## What the live test showed

Driving the app with chrome-devtools MCP (1440×900, real mic, permission granted):

- **Token + WebRTC handshake:** `POST /api/openai/token` → **200** (returns `ek_…`, confirms `gpt-realtime-2`), then `POST https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls` → **201**.
- **Session config applied:** ARIA greeted **in-character** — *"Hi, I'm Aria, and I'm glad you're here…"* — proving `session.update` pushed the persona voice + instructions before first audio.
- **Event stream (instrumented the `oai-events` channel):** `session.created`/`updated`, 133 `response.output_audio_transcript.delta`, `response.done`, plus `input_audio_buffer.speech_started`×4 and `conversation.item.truncated`×2 (barge-in working), and `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta`/`.completed` (whisper user transcripts arriving).
- **Mute** (no barge-in while muted) and **clean teardown** on hang-up (→ ENDED → "Call") both confirmed.
- Console clean except a pre-existing THREE.js deprecation warning.

## The bug I found and fixed

The transcript drawer stayed at **"0 TURNS"** even though captions streamed. Root cause: my `setTurns((prev) => …)` updaters **mutated refs inside the updater** (`agentTurnIdRef.current = newId`, `turnSeqRef.current++`). Next dev runs **React StrictMode**, which **double-invokes state updaters** to surface impurity — the second invocation saw the already-set ref and took the `prev.map` no-op branch on an empty array, discarding every new turn. `setCaption`/`setCallState` use plain values, so they were unaffected — which is why caption updated but turns didn't.

Fix: made the updaters pure (compute id / bump the sequence *before* `setTurns`, pass an updater that only reads `prev`). After the fix the drawer correctly shows **"1 TURNS"** with the agent greeting rendered. I applied the same fix to [use-xai-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-xai-session.ts) — it had the identical latent bug ([use-openai-session.ts](lib/realtime/use-openai-session.ts) was the one under test).

All four gates re-pass after the changes: `tsc` → `lint` → `fmt:check` → `build`.

User-turn *rendering* — the room was quiet during the unmuted window, so no clean user turn was produced live. I've reviewed the VAD guide against our implementation. Here's the finding:

## What we currently send

We **always** send `session.audio.input.turn_detection` as a tuned `server_vad` object — we never set it to `null` or omit it. That part is correct: for a hands-free conversational agent you *want* VAD on (null/omit means manual push-to-talk + `input_audio_buffer.commit`, which isn't this UX). So the structure is right; the problem is **tuning** and a **gap in what we expose**.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **`threshold` is the sensitivity lever** (0–1): *"A higher threshold will require louder audio to activate… might perform better in noisy environments."* Our presets sit at **0.4–0.6** (SNAPPY 0.6 / RELAXED 0.5 / PATIENT 0.4) — at or below OpenAI's 0.5 default, i.e. on the sensitive side. This matches what we saw in testing: ARIA kept reacting to ambient room noise.
- **`semantic_vad`** is OpenAI's purpose-built answer to over-triggering: it chunks on whether the user *semantically* finished a thought, so it's *"less likely to interrupt the user"* and ignores stray noise/fillers. Tuned via `eagerness` (low/medium/high/auto), not `threshold`.
- **Gap in our config type:** `OpenaiAgentConfig.turnDetection` only models `threshold`/`silence_duration_ms`/`prefix_padding_ms`. It can't express `eagerness`, `create_response`, or `interrupt_response` — so semantic VAD isn't actually configurable yet even though the `type` union allows it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

So: not a null/omit bug — a sensitivity-tuning choice. There are two good ways to fix it, with different feel:

## Answer to your question
No — we were **not** setting `turn_detection` to `null` or omitting it. We always sent a `server_vad` object, which is the *correct* posture for a hands-free conversational agent (null/omit means manual push-to-talk + `input_audio_buffer.commit`). - Our `server_vad` thresholds were **0.4–0.6** — at/below OpenAI's 0.5 default, so room noise kept tripping turn detection (exactly the "ARIA keeps reacting to ambient noise" behavior we saw in testing).
- A real gap: the `turnDetection` **type couldn't even express** `eagerness` / `create_response` / `interrupt_response`, so `semantic_vad` wasn't actually configurable despite the `type` union allowing it.

## What I changed (per your choice: semantic_vad)
In [lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts](lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts):
- Added a `VadEagerness` type and **extended** `turnDetection` to fully model both modes: `eagerness` (semantic), `threshold`/`silence_duration_ms`/`prefix_padding_ms` (server), plus `create_response`/`interrupt_response`.

`use-openai-session.ts` already forwards `agent.turnDetection` straight into `session.audio.input.turn_detection`, so no hook change was needed.
